text.p: Former test captain Allan Border, the highest aggregate run scorer in the history of test cricket, was appointed coach of Australia's limited overs reserve side on Tuesday.
Border will also take charge of Australia's under-19 team on their tour to Pakistan in February and March, the Australian Cricket Board announced on Tuesday.

Border, who retired from first-class cricket in 1994, will coach the Australia A side in two limited overs matches against tourists West Indies in Melbourne on December 13 and Pakistan in Sydney on December 28.
The gritty 41-year-old left-handed batsman scored 11,174 runs at an average of 50.56 in 156 tests during an international career spanning more than 15 years.
He captained Australia in a record 93 consecutive tests.
